problems_heading_template: Smoke alarm situations we handle every week in {city_name}
problems_intro_template: Here are the calls {owner_first_name} gets most often from {city_name} homeowners. If your situation matches one of these, you're in the right place.

problem_cards.title: Battery-only smoke alarms chirping or expired
problem_cards.body: Battery-only alarms expire after 10 years (sealed-battery models) or need battery replacement annually. If yours are chirping, yellowed, or you can't remember when they were installed, they're due. We can replace them with hardwired interconnected units so all alarms sound together — the code-required standard for new construction and renovations.

problem_cards.title: Upgrading to hardwired interconnected alarms
problem_cards.body: Older homes often have standalone battery-only alarms that don't communicate with each other. If a downstairs alarm triggers, the upstairs bedrooms hear nothing. Hardwired interconnected alarms wire together on a single circuit — when one triggers, all sound throughout the house. We run the wiring, install the alarms, and test every unit.

problem_cards.title: Smoke alarm code compliance for a home sale
problem_cards.body: When you sell a home in Virginia, the buyer's inspector will flag non-compliant smoke alarms — missing from bedrooms, expired units, or non-interconnected systems. Getting compliant before listing avoids last-minute inspection delays. We assess the house, install what's needed, and give you documentation for the listing agent.

problem_cards.title: Adding carbon monoxide detectors
problem_cards.body: Virginia code requires CO detectors on every level of a dwelling with a fuel-burning appliance or an attached garage. Many homes have smoke alarms but no CO detectors, or have standalone CO detectors that aren't interconnected with the smoke alarms. We install combination smoke/CO units that cover both requirements in one device.

problem_cards.title: Post-renovation smoke alarm placement
problem_cards.body: A finished basement, a new bedroom, or a major remodel triggers code requirements for smoke alarms in the new space. We add hardwired alarms in the new areas and integrate them with the existing system so the whole house is connected.

problem_cards.title: False alarms from old or poorly placed detectors
problem_cards.body: Smoke alarms that trigger every time you cook, run the shower, or open the oven are usually either too close to the kitchen/bathroom or past their 10-year life. We relocate and replace with modern units that have better nuisance-alarm resistance while still meeting code placement requirements.

process_heading_template: Our installation process — what happens when you call
process_intro_template: When you call {phone_display} or request a quote online, here's what happens.

process_steps.title: We assess your current setup
process_steps.body: We ask about your home — how many levels, how many bedrooms, whether you have hardwired or battery-only alarms, and whether you have gas appliances or an attached garage (triggers CO detector requirements). For phone quotes on straightforward replacements, this is enough. For upgrades to hardwired interconnected, we visit.

process_steps.title: On-site assessment for hardwired upgrades
process_steps.body: We walk the house, count alarm locations, check attic/crawl access for running wire, and assess the circuit. You get a written estimate covering the alarm units, the wiring, and the labor. No surprise pricing.

process_steps.title: Installation — typically 2-4 hours for a full house
process_steps.body: For a standard 3-4 bedroom home, hardwired interconnected smoke/CO installation takes 2-4 hours. We run the wiring, mount each alarm, connect them, and test every unit — individually and as a system (triggering one to verify all sound). We label each alarm's manufacture date for the 10-year replacement cycle.

process_steps.title: Testing and documentation
process_steps.body: We test every alarm, verify interconnection, and provide a written record of what was installed, where, and when. This documentation is useful for home insurance, for the next buyer's inspection, and for the 10-year replacement schedule.

pricing_items: Battery-only replacement (no wiring change). Per-alarm pricing, quoted over the phone. We carry Kidde, First Alert, and BRK units on the truck — most replacements finish in one visit.
Hardwired interconnected upgrade (full house). Depends on the number of alarms, wiring access, and home layout. A standard 3-4 bedroom home takes 2-4 hours. Written estimate after on-site assessment.
Single-room additions (post-renovation). Per-alarm pricing plus the wiring run to tie into the existing circuit. Quoted on-site after we see the access path.
Code-compliance assessment. We walk the house, identify what's needed for Virginia fire code compliance, and provide a written quote. No charge for the assessment in our primary service area.
